content: 1. Magnesium oxide and conjugated synthetic estrogens: Conjugated synthetic estrogens reduce magnesium oxide levels by causing a shift of magnesium from the bloodstream into tissue storage. The clinical significance of this interaction is currently unknown. 2. Magnesium oxide and estrified estrogens: Estrified estrogens decrease magnesium oxide levels by promoting the redistribution of magnesium from the blood to tissue storage. The clinical relevance of this effect remains unclear. 3. Magnesium oxide and estropipate: Estropipate reduces magnesium oxide levels by facilitating the transfer of magnesium from the bloodstream to tissue storage. The significance of this interaction is not well established. 4. Magnesium oxide and ethacrynic acid: Ethacrynic acid decreases magnesium oxide levels by increasing renal clearance of magnesium. The clinical importance of this interaction is uncertain. 5. Magnesium oxide and furosemide: Furosemide lowers magnesium oxide levels by enhancing renal excretion of magnesium. The clinical significance of this effect is unknown. 6. Magnesium oxide and gentamicin: Gentamicin reduces magnesium oxide levels by increasing renal clearance of magnesium. The clinical relevance of this interaction is not well defined. 7. Magnesium oxide and glucagon (intranasal): Intranasal glucagon increases magnesium oxide levels by decreasing renal clearance of magnesium. The clinical significance of this interaction is unclear. 8. Magnesium oxide and hydrochlorothiazide: Hydrochlorothiazide decreases magnesium oxide levels by promoting renal excretion of magnesium. The clinical importance of this effect is not well understood. 9. Magnesium oxide and ibandronate: Magnesium oxide reduces the levels of ibandronate by inhibiting its gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is uncertain. 10. Magnesium oxide and indapamide: Indapamide decreases magnesium oxide levels by increasing renal clearance of magnesium. The clinical relevance of this interaction is unknown. 11. Magnesium oxide and mannitol: Mannitol reduces magnesium oxide levels by enhancing renal clearance of magnesium. The clinical significance of this effect is unclear. 12. Magnesium oxide and mestranol: Mestranol decreases magnesium oxide levels by causing a shift of magnesium from the bloodstream into tissue storage. The clinical importance of this interaction is not well established. 13. Magnesium oxide and metolazone: Metolazone lowers magnesium oxide levels by increasing renal excretion of magnesium. The clinical significance of this interaction is uncertain. 14. Magnesium oxide and neomycin (oral): Oral neomycin reduces magnesium oxide levels by enhancing renal clearance of magnesium. The clinical relevance of this effect is not well defined. 15. Magnesium oxide and nitrofurantoin: Magnesium oxide decreases nitrofurantoin levels by inhibiting its gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is unclear. 16. Magnesium oxide and paromomycin: Paromomycin reduces magnesium oxide levels by increasing renal clearance of magnesium. The clinical importance of this interaction is not well understood. 17. Magnesium oxide and sodium polystyrene sulfonate: Sodium polystyrene sulfonate increases magnesium oxide levels by decreasing renal clearance of magnesium. This interaction may increase the risk of alkalosis. The clinical significance is uncertain. 18. Magnesium oxide and spironolactone: Spironolactone increases magnesium oxide levels by reducing renal clearance of magnesium. The clinical relevance of this interaction is unclear. 19. Magnesium oxide and streptomycin: Streptomycin decreases magnesium oxide levels by enhancing renal clearance of magnesium. The clinical significance of this effect is not well established. 20. Magnesium oxide and tobramycin: Tobramycin reduces magnesium oxide levels by increasing renal excretion of magnesium. The clinical importance of this interaction is uncertain. 21. Magnesium oxide and torsemide: Torsemide decreases magnesium oxide levels by promoting renal clearance of magnesium. The clinical relevance of this effect is unclear. 22. Magnesium oxide and triamterene: Triamterene increases magnesium oxide levels by decreasing renal clearance of magnesium. The clinical significance of this interaction is not well defined. 23. Magnesium oxide and acalabrutinib: Magnesium oxide reduces the levels and efficacy of acalabrutinib by increasing gastric pH, which decreases the solubility of acalabrutinib. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. It is recommended to separate the administration of acalabrutinib and antacids by at least 2 hours. Therapy modification or close monitoring is advised. 24. Magnesium oxide and atazanavir: Magnesium oxide decreases the levels and efficacy of atazanavir by increasing gastric pH, which reduces the solubility of atazanavir. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. It is recommended to administer atazanavir 2 hours before or 1 hour after antacids. Alternative therapy should be considered. 25. Magnesium oxide and baloxavir marboxil: Magnesium oxide reduces the levels of baloxavir marboxil by binding to cations in the gastrointestinal tract, which decreases its absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Alternative therapy is recommended.
